title: Magnetotail
definition: A planetary magnetosphere has a part pushed in the direction of the solar wind, called the magnetotail.[^1] NOAA explains the shape: the pressure of the solar wind compresses Earth’s field on the dayside and stretches it into a long tail on the nightside, which extends to hundreds of Earth radii.[^2] ESA lists the magnetotail, together with the polar cusps, as a key region its Cluster spacecraft visited to study how the solar wind interacts with the magnetosphere.[^1]
